chunks.title: LinkedIn post 9 (1/4)
chunks.text: A few days back, I learned something without even participating in a hackathon 😄 There was a Google Developer Groups (GDG) hackathon at our university. I didn’t take part — no team, tight schedule. A day before, a classmate asked: 👉 which AI IDE I use 👉 what I use for frontend & backend ⚛️ React 🔥 Firebase 🤖 Antigravity The next day at 5:30 PM while I was in library(rare 😅), he asked how to deploy. I explained the Vercel flow. Around 7 PM, while I was still in the library (very rare 😅), I got a call: “Vercel isn’t recognizing the repo and we need to submit till 8-9 pm.” So I walked to the reading area in the opposite building — and instantly saw the issue 👀 The project was uploaded as a ZIP file 📦 Then I asked: “Do you have Git installed?” The answer was: “I don’t know.

chunks.title: LinkedIn post 9 (2/4)
chunks.text: e 👀 The project was uploaded as a ZIP file 📦 Then I asked: “Do you have Git installed?” The answer was: “I don’t know.” I installed Git , pushed the repo properly, and deployed — live 🚀 I also guided them on backend deployment using Render for later. This wasn’t just one team — I helped with the same issue 3–5 teams that evening(all teams present there). Most were 8–9.5 CGPA rankers. I’m a 7.15 CGPA struggler 😅 That day made one thing clear: fundamentals beat last-minute cramming. Even if the scores are lower. Even if the journey is slower. Because when it’s time to build, debug, deploy, and fix things under pressure — fundamentals show up.
